AC Milan welcome Serie A surprise package Frosinone to the San Siro, with the promoted side arriving just four points behind their hosts.

Match News and Current Form

Milan have lost just once in Serie A this term (W7, D3), establishing themselves as potential title contenders under Ruben Amorim, albeit they’re already playing catch-up on that front. Their gap to the summit would’ve been even wider had they not beaten Inter Milan 3-1 in their last home league outing, a result which continued their impressive pattern of scoring at least twice in all five of their home league games this season (W4, L1). Continuing that impressive run here could be easier said than done here, as the Rossoneri have only won three of their last seven league fixtures immediately after an international break (D2, L2).

Frosinone have made light work of the step up from Serie B (W6, D2, L3), and they could become just the fourth promoted side in the last 40 years to win seven of their opening 12 Serie A fixtures of the season. Massimiliano Alvini’s attack-minded side have earned their shot at history by outscoring even Milan (24-23), although their momentum was halted with a 3-1 defeat to Cagliari on matchday 11 which ended a four-match unbeaten run (W3, D1). Bouncing back on the road appears a tall order for the Canaries, who are winless in four away league games (D2, L2) since beating Fiorentina 3-0 on matchday two. 

Head-to-Head History

Milan are unbeaten across all six previous H2Hs (W4, D2), scoring at least twice in each of their three home meetings (W2, D1).

Milan could be without as many as seven players here, while Frosinone’s Antonio Raimondo is injured and Gabriele Bracaglia is suspended.

Match News and Current Form

Racing’s 2-1 triumph over Málaga propelled them into La Liga’s top ten ahead of this round of fixtures and was their second win from their last three top-flight games (L1), as many wins as they had achieved in their previous 29 such matches. The Basque side should not be bothered by the pressure of playing away from home, having won three of their last four such league games (L1) - as many victories as in their previous 25 top-flight matches on their travels. Getafe’s form at home has been the sole reason they’ve been able to stay out of the bottom three but that record will be tested by Atlético Madrid, as boss Diego Simeone pursues a historic victory.

Match News and Current Form

The international break appeared to come at an appropriate time for Getafe after manager José Bordalás blamed fatigue for a fadeout at Villarreal in which they conceded twice after the 75th minute to lose 2-0. Few clubs in Europe’s top-five leagues have endured such an enormous disparity between their home and away form quite like Getafe, who are outside of the relegation zone only by way of collecting all 12 of their points at the Estadio Coliseum (W3, D3), where they are now on their longest unbeaten run in this competition (W5, D3) since a run of 11 games in 2023 (W7, D4).

Atlético Madrid were left to wonder what might have been after Giuliano Simeone’s tenth-minute opener was cancelled out on the way to a 2-1 loss at home to Barcelona that saw them spend the international break five points from the summit, instead of at its peak. Diego Simeone would not criticise his players for denying him a record-breaking 345th La Liga victory, particularly as the club are still enjoying their equal-best start to a league campaign since they last won the title in 2020/21. Now the focus is on registering a fifth consecutive away win in this competition for the third time in Simeone’s long tenure, having previously done so in 2021 and 2014. 

Head-to-Head History

Getafe collected points from three of the last seven La Liga H2Hs (W1, D2, L4), but the success has been modest and short-lived. Diego Simeone could equal Luis Aragonés’ La Liga record for most wins against one opposition with what would be a 23rd win over Getafe here (D4, L1).

Match News and Current Form

Juventus started to trend upwards before the international break, losing just one of their last six matches in all competitions (W3, D2) after twice coming from behind to draw 2-2 at Fiorentina. Pressure has therefore started to lift off Luciano Spalletti, who becomes only the sixth manager to take charge of 600 Serie A matches here and will be confident of marking the occasion in style given that the Bianconeri have collected 22 of a possible 24 points across their last eight league games against newly-promoted clubs. Scoring 21 times overall while conceding just once in the last six matches of that sequence highlights Juventus’ dominance in such games, and losing just once at home this term (W4, D2) further underlines their favourites tag here.

Venezia recorded a valuable 2-1 home victory over fellow strugglers Udinese before the international break, snapping a three-match losing streak to climb off the bottom of the table. Just two wins from their opening 11 rounds and a league-low eight goals scored suggests that survival specialist manager Davide Nicola still faces a tough task, with the Winged Lions last winning back-to-back Serie A games in November 2021. Claiming three points on the road won't be easy either, as Venezia have lost their last six top-flight away matches, and could suffer seven successive Serie A road defeats for the first time since 2001 here.

Juventus have won seven of their last nine outings against Venezia (D2), despite conceding in each of the last five. The Bianconeri have scored 2+ goals in six of their last seven home league H2Hs.
